ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: On June 19, 2017, during the process of launching the Zhongxing 9A satellite by the Long March 3B Y28 rocket, an incident occurred. Due to an anomaly of the launch vehicle, the satellite did not enter the predetermined orbit according to the original plan. Through the cooperation and efforts of aerospace tracking, telemetry and command personnel, and through multiple orbital adjustments, the satellite successfully changed orbit and entered a geostationary satellite orbit. The schematic diagram of the satellite orbit-change principle is shown in the figure. The satellite changes speed at the apogee Q of elliptical orbit I and enters geostationary orbit II. Point P is the perigee of the elliptical orbit. Which of the following statements is correct ( )
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The speed of the satellite at point Q on elliptical orbit I is less than the speed at point Q on geostationary orbit II

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an outer circular orbit, labeled II; inside the circle there is an elliptical orbit, labeled I. The Earth is drawn at a position inside the elliptical orbit and to the left, P is marked near the left side of the ellipse, Q is marked on the right side, and Q is the apogee of elliptical orbit I, while also lying on the outer circular orbit II. The question stem says that the satellite changes speed at the apogee Q of elliptical orbit I and enters geostationary orbit II, so what is compared is the speed at the same spatial position Q when the satellite moves respectively along elliptical orbit I and circular geostationary orbit II. Reasoning: Let the distance from Q to the geocenter be r_Q. Geostationary orbit II at Q can be regarded as a circular orbit with radius r_Q, so its speed satisfies v_Ⅱ^2=GM/r_Q. Elliptical orbit I has Q as the apogee, the apogee radius is r_Q, and the semi-major axis a_I of the ellipse is less than the apogee radius r_Q. From the vis-viva equation v^2=GM(2/r-1/a), the speed of elliptical orbit I at point Q satisfies v_Ⅰ^2=GM(2/r_Q-1/a_I). Because a_I<r_Q, so 1/a_I>1/r_Q, and thus 2/r_Q-1/a_I < 1/r_Q; therefore v_Ⅰ^2<v_Ⅱ^2, namely v_Ⅰ<v_Ⅱ.
